newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco airport panel OKs $2.4 bln expansion.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco airport panel OKs $2.4 bln expansion.

text.p: The San Francisco Airports Commission on Tuesday approved a $2.4 billion, revenue bond-financed plan to expand the city's airport.
As part of the plan, up to $300 million of revenue bonds will be sold competitively in October, followed by other bond issues over the next several years, airport officials said.

The final budget for the San Francisco International Airport expansion is $346 million higher than earlier estimates. The revised budget takes into account rising steel prices, increasing security requirements, unexpectedly high bids from contractors and additional underground work.
John Martin, director of airports, called the revised budget and schedule "reasonable, achievable and prudent".
The $2.4 billion total includes $376 million in contingencies and reserves, airport officials said.
The $2.4 billion figure does not include borrowing costs.

If all goes as planned, construction will be financed almost exclusively with airport revenue bonds. Over $760 million in bonds have already been sold toward the project. Up to $300 million of bonds are expected to be sold in October. The rest will be sold over the next four years.
All of the bonds are expected to be issued competitively.
The airport is planning a two million sq ft international terminal, new roadways, an elevated rail shuttle and new parking structures.

The master plan construction programme is projected to generate 3,500 full-time construction jobs and $43 million in local tax revenue, including $10 million to San Francisco and $13 million to San Mateo County, the airport said.

San Francisco International Airport ranks fifth among U.S. airports and eighth worldwide on the basis of passenger volume. About 38 million air passengers use San Francisco International airport every year and experts predict that the number will increase to 51 million by the year 2006.
